title: Other saxophonists: Wayne King, Rudy Wiedoft, Leonard Fields
summary: Carter discusses saxophonists whose sound or technique impressed him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: What about any other saxophonist that might have made an impression on you, and, of course, we’re talking about 1923 or ’24. Really, it’s hard to think who might have been around.

Well, you know, I can’t remember that there was anybody that influenced me. I know that I used to like the sound of Wayne King, the instrument, you know, the sound he got out of the instrument, and he was the melody player. Gee, I don’t know.
Some quote, unquote “jazz musicians” have mentioned that Rudy Wiedoft inspired them, not what he was playing so much as just what could be done on the instrument. Do you remember him?

Oh, definitely. He let you know what could be done on the instrument, and he let you know that he could do it, you know. It was purely technique, which was a dazzling technique for the time. Gee, I mean, there was also a player around at that time that I think came from Lexington, Kentucky, another one that nobody around today would probably remember or would have heard of, and his name was Leonard Fields, and he was a fantastic player. Gee, he got over the instrument like crazy and, gee, I don’t know that he ever recorded. If he did, I’d like to find the recording.
